transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Okonkwo, thank you for coming back in to see me today. I asked you here because I have some important information regarding your grandson's visit yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is something wrong with the boy? He seemed fine when we left.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I wish I could say that, but there was a medical error during his vaccinations. We gave him a dose of the vaccine intended for an older, heavier child, rather than the dose meant for his specific weight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. What does that mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means he received more of the medication than he should have. We used the wrong weight band when drawing up the injection. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose so. But why are you telling me this now? He is a healthy baby.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a lot to take in. This is a very difficult conversation to have, and I want to make sure we address every concern you have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Now, look, children get reactions. He might have been a bit fussy, or perhaps it is just how he is reacting to the illness he had last month. Surely this is just the natural way things go.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion about the dosage, but this wasn't a natural reaction. This was a mistake made by our team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You say mistake, but my family is known in this community. If people think the child was harmed because of a mistake, it reflects on us. On my position. Maybe it is better to just say he had a strong reaction.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that the community's perception matters.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is more than that. My reputation is built on stability.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: If the boy is fine, why dwell on it? If he is a bit sluggish today, it is because he is a baby.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: While I hear you, the fact remains that the wrong dose was administered. I am sorry that this happened. We were very busy in the clinic yesterday and the wrong vial was selected.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Busy. You are telling me my grandson was given the wrong medicine because you were busy?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is how it happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is very distressing. I cannot have the elders asking why I brought my grandson to a clinic that makes such errors.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do you actually know if he is in danger?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Based on the specific vaccine, the risk of a serious adverse reaction is low, but we need to monitor him. To make sure you are clear on the situation, can you tell me what you've understood about the error?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You gave him a dose for a bigger child. Because you were rushed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still think you are overreacting. He is a strong boy. He will grow out of it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I appreciate your confidence in him. However, the medical fact is that the dosage was incorrect.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And now? What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Here is the plan. First, I want you to bring him back tomorrow morning at 9 AM for a weight and temperature check. I will perform that exam myself.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow? I have a meeting with the council.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I recognize that is a conflict, but it is the necessary next step for his safety. After that exam, I will provide you with a written summary of the event and the monitoring plan. You should watch for any unusual rashes or extreme lethargy tonight; if you see those, call my direct line immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the records? Will this be on his permanent file?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, it will be documented accurately. I will also be filing an incident report to our quality board so we can change how vaccines are drawn to ensure this doesn't happen to another child.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want people knowing this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that is a worry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is a shame.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. So, we have the appointment for 9 AM tomorrow, and you will call me if he develops a rash or becomes too sleepy. Do we have an agreement on those steps?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. I will bring him. But I am not happy about this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I completely understand that you are not happy. We will see you tomorrow.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts the patient, remains regulated despite pushback regarding reputation and the clinic's errors, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: The error is named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and a comprehension check is performed once ('can you tell me what you've understood').

A.justification: While direct apologies are used, the resident dilutes accountability by offering the excuse that they 'were very busy in the clinic yesterday'.

R.justification: The resident relies on generic validation ('I understand', 'I see') without naming specific emotions or engaging deeply with the patient's distress over his reputation.

T.justification: The plan includes a specific next step with a timeline (tomorrow at 9 AM), a named patient role (bring him back, watch for rashes), and a prevention strategy (incident report to quality board).
